methods.name: cutover.mayServe
methods.summary: May the core serve this module now? Read-only gate over the cutover switch: `{ok, warning}`. `ok` needs the module's switch file, the marker `step` left in the core and its tombstones; an env opt-in changes nothing once the file exists. Owner and Host may ask (the host's start guard calls it as the Host principal); it writes nothing.

params.summary: The cutover module (`kith migrate status` lists them).

methods.name: run.mint
methods.summary: A run token for one run of an agent, for a person in a conversation (and the claim it holds, when it holds one). The token is shown once; it works on the run socket only for a peer that descends from the process bound with run.bind. Tokens live in the daemon's memory and are gone when it restarts, and when the person (or the owner of a bot) is suspended or removed; a mint for a revoked person is refused. The answer also names the run socket (`socket`).

params.name: agent
params.summary: The agent the run is of.

params.name: person
params.summary: The invited person or bot guest the run is for.

params.name: conversation
params.summary: The conversation the run continues.

params.name: claim
params.summary: The writer claim the run holds (kept in the identity; claims themselves are M3).

params.name: room
params.summary: The room, when the run is in one.

params.name: project
params.summary: The project the run was launched in.

methods.summary: The cards waiting (oldest first) and the owner's recent closed ones (newest first), as `{open, recent}`.

methods.name: cards.answer
methods.summary: Answers a card. Answers `{result: answered}` (with the card's new state), `closed` (it was already answered, withdrawn or expired), `expired` (its time ran out first) or `claimed` (another answerer holds it). Refuses a secret card (a key or access ask: answer it in the Kith app), an unknown card and an answer the card does not offer.

params.name: id
params.summary: The card.

params.name: answer
params.summary: The answer: one of the card's option ids, or allow, deny or cancel when it lists none.

methods.name: cards.provide
methods.summary: Types a key into a key card: the core claims the card, seals every value into the secrets envelope and spends the card in one commit, at most once. Answers `{result: saved}` (names only: the service, account and variables, never a value), `closed` (answered, denied, saved or withdrawn already), `expired` (its time ran out first) or `claimed` (another provide holds it). A failed write changes nothing and leaves the card open. Refuses a card that is not a key card, an account name that is taken or unusable, and values that do not match the card. The values are never logged or echoed; a terminal does not type them, an app fills them in.

params.name: id
params.summary: The key card.

params.name: account
params.summary: The account name for a new key (the card names it when it replaces one).

params.name: values
params.summary: The key's fields by variable name. Never written on a command line.

params.name: name
params.summary: The secret's name.

params.name: value

params.name: holder

params.name: rt

params.name: max
params.summary: How many slots there are (1 or more). Remembered; later takes may leave it out.

params.name: invitee

params.name: pid
params.summary: The holder's process (2 or more), so a crash frees the slot.

methods.name: gate.release
methods.summary: Gives a slot or a place in line back. Releasing a holder that holds nothing does nothing.

params.summary: The run or claim.

methods.name: gate.park

params.name: holder
params.summary: The run or claim.

methods.name: gate.unpark

params.name: holder
params.summary: The run or claim.

methods.name: syncLease.status
methods.summary: Whether this Mac is in sync with the cloud. Answers `cloud` (`unknown`, `linked` or `off`), `synced`, `held` (what a non-owner's claim needs: the cloud is off, or linked with the lease unexpired), `until` (ms) and `mark`.

methods.name: syncLease.link
methods.summary: The cloud is on: the lease decides from now on, and it is not held until a pull says so. Linking again changes nothing.

methods.name: syncLease.unlink
methods.summary: The cloud is off on purpose: nothing waits on it, and any lease is gone.

methods.name: syncLease.mark
methods.summary: Where the cloud's changes stand. Take it before a pull reads the cloud's state, and give it back to `syncLease.pulled`.

methods.name: syncLease.changed
methods.summary: The cloud said its state changed: the lease ends at once, until a pull that started after this succeeds. Answers the new `mark`.

methods.name: syncLease.drop
methods.summary: The connection to the cloud dropped or is being made: the lease ends. Dropping when nothing is held does nothing.

methods.name: syncLease.pulled
methods.summary: A pull of the cloud's state succeeded. Answers `held: true` when the lease now runs, `held: false` when it does not: the cloud changed since the mark, the cloud is not linked, or the clock is behind its last reading.

params.name: mark
params.summary: The `mark` taken before the pull read the cloud's state.

params.name: ms
params.summary: How long the lease runs, 1 to 3600000 (120000 when absent).

methods.name: syncLease.renew
methods.summary: The relay was heard: runs a held lease out again. Answers `renewed: true`, or `renewed: false` when nothing is held to renew (never acquired, lost, expired or the clock is behind): only a pull acquires.

params.name: ms
params.summary: How long the lease runs from now, 1 to 3600000 (120000 when absent).

Answers the door (`state` starting, its `version`) and `repeat` (true when this id was already starting or live, nothing written). params.name: version

Answers `swept` (this call's) and `pending` (swept before, box not confirmed gone). The owner is never swept by a name, only for a gone supervisor. Kills nothing.

methods.summary: The conversations, newest first, with the engine, the account and whether a writer holds each.

params.summary: The conversation.

methods.summary: The writer claims: the live ones (queued, claimed, running) and the recent ended ones, as `{live, recent}`.

methods.name: schedule.preview
methods.summary: The next fires of a trigger, as `{fires: [{at, iso}]}` (`at` in ms since the epoch): `{type: cron, expr, tz}` (tz `local` or an IANA zone), `{type: interval, every}` (seconds), `{type: once, at}`; a webhook or event has none. Refuses a spec `kith-sched` refuses, with its message.

params.name: trigger
params.summary: The trigger, as JSON (`{"type":"cron","expr":"0 9 * * 1-5","tz":"Europe/Paris"}`).

params.name: after
params.summary: Fires after this time, ms since the epoch (now by default).

params.name: n
params.summary: How many fires (5 by default, at most 100).

methods.name: schedule.jobs
methods.summary: Every job of every agent with its next run and its last run, from jobs.json and the core's run state. Also says which agents' files could not be read, the runs of jobs since removed, and the last tick.

params.name: agent
params.summary: Only this agent's.

methods.name: schedule.show
methods.summary: One job in full: its definition, next run, last run, recent runs and recent fires. Refuses an agent or job that does not exist.

params.name: agent
params.summary: The agent.

params.name: id
params.summary: The job.

methods.name: schedule.next
methods.summary: The jobs that are not paused, soonest first, with when each runs next.

params.name: agent
params.summary: Only this agent's.

methods.name: schedule.tick
methods.summary: Fire what is due at `now` (the caller's clock, ms; this machine's by default): one transaction per job that writes its fire row, its turn and the watermark. Catch-up fires only the latest due slot inside a day; older ones are kept as one `skipped:missed` row. Nothing runs this on a clock yet: `kith-sched` owns jobs.json until M4-5.

params.name: now
params.summary: The clock, ms since the epoch (this machine's by default).

methods.name: schedule.runNow
methods.summary: Run a job now through the same fire: it obeys the skip rule. A busy job answers `busy` and writes nothing, so a retry fires once it is free; a `key` that was decided answers what was decided; a paused or revoked job answers final.

params.name: agent
params.summary: The agent.

params.name: id
params.summary: The job.

params.name: key
params.summary: The run's own key (letters, digits, - _ .); a retry with the same key is the same run.

params.name: now
params.summary: The clock, ms since the epoch (this machine's by default).

methods.name: schedule.fire
methods.summary: A webhook or event delivery for one job: checks the job's key (`Authorization: Bearer` or a GitHub-style `X-Hub-Signature-256` HMAC of the exact body, the key read from the secrets lane), the event against the job's trigger and filters, then fires through the same transaction as `schedule.runNow` with the slot `event:<hash of the delivery id>`, so a redelivery fires at most once. Answers `fired`, `busy` (retry), `ignored`, `ping`, `refused` (`unauthorized`, `paused`, `gone`, `invalid`) or what an earlier delivery of the same id decided. The body is UTF-8 text: the listener refuses a body that is not as `invalid` and never converts it lossily (a replaced byte would make a correct signature fail). The host calls it as itself with the real sender in `caller`; `caller` is only echoed in the answer, never used to decide anything, and M4-5 stores it with the fire row.

params.name: agent
params.summary: The agent.

params.name: id
params.summary: The job.

params.name: headers
params.summary: The request headers, name to value.

params.name: body
params.summary: The exact request body (text).

params.name: caller
params.summary: Who sent it, as the host knows (the real principal). Echoed, never used to decide.

methods.name: conversation.transcript
methods.summary: The engine sessions a conversation has, one per account: the engine, its session id, the pointer to where the engine keeps it, the hash and size as of the last read, and whether the engine's copy is there now and has changed since. Refuses an id that is no conversation. Only Claude's sessions are held; another engine's row says `held: false`.

params.name: id
params.summary: The conversation.

params.name: account
params.summary: Only this account's session (`claude`, `claude:work`).

methods.name: wake.enqueue
methods.summary: Asks for a turn of a session. Answers `result`: `queued`, `merged` (the session was already owed something: one turn carries both) or `duplicate` (the id is queued, answered or withdrawn: dropped). Refuses a person's session on the run door, and a session that is another person's or agent's.

params.name: session
params.summary: The session to wake.

params.name: id
params.summary: The request's id; one already queued, answered or withdrawn is dropped.

params.name: agent
params.summary: The agent whose session it is.

params.name: person
params.summary: The person the session serves (needs `--door host`).

params.name: room
params.summary: The room it was asked in.

params.name: door
params.summary: `run` (the kernel resumes the session; the default) or `host` (the host runs the turn).

params.name: why
params.summary: A few words on what happened.

params.name: text
params.summary: What the session is told.

methods.name: wake.withdraw
methods.summary: Stop: drops what a session is still owed (not what a running turn already holds), keeping the ids so a late copy is dropped; without `--id` its waiters go too. Answers `count`.

params.name: session
params.summary: The session.

params.name: id
params.summary: Only this request.

methods.name: wake.withdrawPerson
methods.summary: Revoke or removal: drops what every session of these people is owed, and those sessions' waiters. Answers `count`.

params.name: persons
params.summary: The people.

methods.name: wake.take
methods.summary: The host starts a host-door turn: marks what a session is owed as carried by this holder and answers `turn` (the turn as `kith-wake take` prints it), or null when nothing is owed. Recovers turns whose holder died first (a turn whose marker is in its transcript is answered, one that is not is owed again). A session a live writer holds is still offered, as in the Python: the host answers `back --held`. Creates no turn in the conversations lane yet.

params.name: holder
params.summary: The holder's process id.

params.name: session
params.summary: Only this session.

params.name: sid
params.summary: The Claude session the turn runs in (default: the session itself, when it is one).

methods.name: wake.done
methods.summary: The turn ended: what it carried is answered (`--how withdrawn`: dropped, not delivered). Answers `done`: false when no turn has that run id.

params.name: run
params.summary: The turn.

params.name: how
params.summary: How it ended (default answered).

methods.name: wake.back
methods.summary: The turn did not start: what it carried is owed again, after a pause that doubles (5 s to 10 min), and after five failed tries it ends as failed. `--held` (a writer had the session) is not a failed try. Answers `done`: false when no turn has that run id.

params.name: run
params.summary: The turn.

params.name: held
params.summary: A writer held the session: owed again soon, not a failed try.

methods.name: wake.queueList
methods.summary: What is owed and what is waited for, as `items` (a queue file each), `waiters` and `lines` (what `kith-wake ls` prints).

methods.name: wake.queueStatus
methods.summary: Where a request is: `queued`, `running`, how it was answered (`answered`, `failed`, `withdrawn`, ...) or `unknown`, and the turn that carried it, as `{id, state, run}`.

params.name: id
params.summary: The request's id.

methods.name: wake.wait
methods.summary: Wakes a session once something happened: `ci:OWNER/REPO#PR` (its checks finished, or it was merged or closed), `pid:N` (the process exited) or `at:TIME` (`+30m`, or a local `2026-10-27T15:00`). A waiter always has a timeout. Waiting twice on the same thing keeps the first waiter. Answers the waiter as `waiter`.

params.name: on
params.summary: What to wait for.

params.name: session
params.summary: The session to wake.

params.name: agent
params.summary: The agent whose session it is.

params.name: why
params.summary: A few words, told to the session when it wakes.

params.name: timeout
params.summary: Give up after this long (default 6h).

params.name: note
params.summary: A note for the session, told when it wakes.

params.name: person
params.summary: The caller's KITH_PERSON (a guest may not set waiters).

params.name: via
params.summary: The caller's KITH_VIA (default terminal).

methods.name: ask.open
methods.summary: Opens an ask: the hop and cost-cap check and the insert of its record in ONE transaction, so no second ask passes the cap between them. Answers `{decision, record}` (the chain, hop and cross hops the record got). A cap that refuses it is an error with the words `kith ask` prints. With `--check-only` nothing is written (`record` is null).

params.name: id
params.summary: The new ask's id.

params.name: asked
params.summary: The agent asked.

params.name: crossing
params.summary: The ask goes to another Mac.

params.name: brief
params.summary: What was asked (at most 2000 characters kept).

params.name: pid
params.summary: The asking process, so a crash is found.

params.name: conversation
params.summary: The asked agent's session of a `--bg` run, when it has one.

params.name: checkOnly
params.summary: Decide, write nothing.

params.name: kernel
params.summary: The kernel folder (default: the one this program finds).

params.name: home
params.summary: The caller's home folder (a daemon has its own).

params.name: env
params.summary: The caller's KITH_* and HQ_* variables (`KITH_ASK_ID`, `KITH_ASK_CHAIN`/`HOP`/`CROSS`/`COST`/`FROM`, `KITH_AGENT`, `KITH_PERSON`, `KITH_VIA`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`); a daemon has its own.

methods.name: ask.settle
methods.summary: The run behind an ask ended a turn at a cost (US$): it joins its chain's cost, and a chain that reaches its cap with this turn is marked once per cap. `--state` answered or stopped settles an open ask (capped when this turn tipped the chain). Settling a settled ask only adds the cost. Answers `{id, state, cost, tipped}`; refuses an id that is no ask.

params.name: id
params.summary: The ask.

params.name: cost
params.summary: US$ this turn cost (a number).

params.name: state
params.summary: answered or stopped; left out while the run waits on a card.

params.name: kernel
params.summary: The kernel folder (default: the one this program finds).

params.name: home
params.summary: The caller's home folder (a daemon has its own).

params.name: env
params.summary: The caller's KITH_* and HQ_* variables (`KITH_ASK_ID`, `KITH_ASK_CHAIN`/`HOP`/`CROSS`/`COST`/`FROM`, `KITH_AGENT`, `KITH_PERSON`, `KITH_VIA`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`); a daemon has its own.

methods.name: ask.capTold
methods.summary: The host raised the chain's cap card: it is not raised again for this cap. Answers `{marked}`, the records marked.

params.name: chain
params.summary: The chain (its root ask's id).

methods.name: ask.end
methods.summary: Stop, revoke, removal (`kith ask --end`): settles `stopped` the asks whose caller is one of the sessions or persons, or that are one of the roots, and every ask below them; stops what each one's conversation runs (queued and parked turns cancelled, the live claim to `ending`, an unspawned one ended); withdraws the wakes and waiters those callers are owed. An ask already delivered or answered to its caller stays. Repeating it is safe. Kills no process: answers `{ended, sessions, kill}` (the ids, the sessions withdrawn, and the writers `{claimId, pid, started}` to kill until gone).

params.name: roots
params.summary: Asks whose whole subtree ends.

params.name: sessions
params.summary: Caller sessions whose asks end.

params.name: persons
params.summary: People whose asks end.

methods.name: ask.to
methods.summary: `kith ask --to ID`, the check before anything is queued: whether the ask still takes a follow-up. An ask that was stopped or ended refuses with `was stopped; ask anew` (the stopped fence never lifts; the Python `--to` queued the message and the wake fence dropped it). Answers `{id, ok}`; refuses an id that is no ask.

params.name: id
params.summary: The ask.

methods.name: ask.revokeEverywhere
methods.summary: The revoke order for conversations, once the authority revoke is visible to the may check: the person's claims and each of their bots' (queued and parked turns cancelled, live claims to `ending`, the revoke epoch bumped so a claim that passed its may check before is refused), THEN the asks of the person and their bots with every ask below them (`ask.end --persons`). `ask.end` alone is not a revoke. One claim transaction per principal, then one for the asks. Safe to repeat; a retry (with the same bots) finishes a crash between the steps, and a crash after the person's step leaves the bots' in-flight claims unfenced until it. On a removal pass `--bots`, read before the write: the rows are gone after. Kills no process: answers `{principals, cancelledTurns, ended, sessions, kill}`.

params.name: person
params.summary: The person revoked.

params.name: bots
params.summary: Bots of the person (the whole transitive set) read before an authority removal deleted their rows; the bots still in `people.bot_of` are added.

methods.name: ask.delegations
methods.summary: `kith ask delegations --json`: every ask record, newest first, as `{delegations}` (money in micro-dollars, times in ms).

params.name: kernel
params.summary: The kernel folder (default: the one this program finds).

params.name: home
params.summary: The caller's home folder (a daemon has its own).

params.name: env
params.summary: The caller's KITH_* and HQ_* variables (`KITH_ASK_ID`, `KITH_ASK_CHAIN`/`HOP`/`CROSS`/`COST`/`FROM`, `KITH_AGENT`, `KITH_PERSON`, `KITH_VIA`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`); a daemon has its own.

methods.name: ask.record
methods.summary: The record of one ask as `kith ask` reads it (an old registration reads as a root ask). Refuses an id that has none.

params.name: id
params.summary: The ask.

methods.name: ask.limits
methods.summary: The delegation caps: hops on one Mac, hops across Macs, the refused exit code, the default cap and `cap_usd`, the chain cap in force (null for none).

params.name: kernel
params.summary: The kernel folder (default: the one this program finds).

params.name: home
params.summary: The caller's home folder (a daemon has its own).

params.name: env
params.summary: The caller's KITH_* and HQ_* variables (`KITH_ASK_ID`, `KITH_ASK_CHAIN`/`HOP`/`CROSS`/`COST`/`FROM`, `KITH_AGENT`, `KITH_PERSON`, `KITH_VIA`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`); a daemon has its own.

methods.name: account.state
methods.summary: What each account is doing: its out mark, usage reading and last start, as `state.json` keeps them, from the core's database. One entry with `--entry`, else all as `{accounts}`.

params.name: entry
params.summary: One account id, such as `claude:work`; answers `{id, state}` (`state` is null when it has no row).

methods.name: account.pick
methods.summary: The accounts a run of the agent would try, in order, reading the core's database for what is out or used least (`kith account pick AGENT --json`): `{candidates, skipped, all_out, harness, policy, pin}`.

params.name: agent
params.summary: The agent.

params.name: agentMd
params.summary: The agent's agent.md, when it is not in the agents folder (the harness comes from it).

params.name: deep
params.summary: Ask each harness whether its login is good, not only look for the folder or the key.

Harness.description: The program an agent runs on: `harness:` in its agent.md (`claude-code` is printed as claude), or a backup entry's. The host starts claude, codex, and any engine of the core's table with an ACP mode (`kith engines`); `agy` is the kernel's word for antigravity. One this version doesn't know is its own state: the host doesn't start it.

RolePrompt.description: How an engine takes the agent's role prompt, from the engine table's `enforces`: `flag` (a flag or ACP option on the command line), `env` (an environment variable), `first-message` (in front of the first message), `none` (not known to be deliverable: the host puts it in front of the first message). One this version doesn't know is read as none.

PermissionMode.description: The Claude Code permission mode a run starts in (kernel/lib/kith_settings.py CHOICES); a Codex run gets the host's translation. One this version doesn't know starts the run in default, which asks before every change.

DelegationState.description: Where a delegation (one `kith ask` id) stands: `open` (running, or parked on a card), `answered`, `capped` (answered, and its run took the chain to its cost cap) or `stopped` (the run gave no answer). One this version doesn't know is its own state: the host leaves it alone.

Agent.description: One agent in `kith ls --json`. `home` is its folder, where its bot works. A kernel from before `harness` was listed runs every agent on Claude. `builtin` is true for an agent that ships with kith (like scratch): never backed up or shared; older kernels leave it out.

NewAgent.description: `kith new <name> <description> --json`: the agent just made. `home` is its folder (memory, data and files beside the role), `dir` its role folder (its own repo: agent.md, settings.json, skills). A failure prints `{"ok": false, "error": "..."}` and exits non-zero instead, and leaves no folder behind.

Projects.description: `kith project ls --json`: every registered project, sorted by id.

Project.description: One registered project: its paths (absolute), its home folder when it has one, its git remotes, the project it sits in, its shared memory folder, and whether a folder of it is on this Mac.

Launch.description: `kith <agent> --launch-json`: how to start the agent, for claude and codex and, additively, any other engine the table lists with an ACP mode: `engine` is the table id (left out for claude and codex, which print what they always did), `acp` the installed CLI's own ACP program (null when it has none here: the host then starts the `registry` build), `role_prompt` how the engine takes `system_prompt`. `settings` is Claude Code's settings (null for another harness), `mcp_servers` its servers in Claude's format, `claude_args` the arguments `kith <agent>` would give claude (null for another harness). `backup`, `provider` and `account` say which backup entry, harness and login answer the run; `account_id` is that login as a backup id (`claude`, `claude:work`, `codex`), the agent's main account or the `--backup` entry.

AcpStart.description: How to start an engine over ACP, from the engine table (`kith kernel engines launch <id> --json`): the installed CLI's own ACP mode as a program. `env` is extra environment for it (the engine's keys are the host's own).

CostTag.description: What the cost ledger files a run's usage under. `via` is where the run came from (terminal, serve, a channel).

Delegations.description: `kith ask delegations --json`: every delegation record on this Mac, newest first.

Delegation.description: The record of one `kith ask` id (foreground, --bg or agent@machine), in kernel/bin/kith-ask's ~/.kith/live/ask/ID.reg. `agent` is the agent asked, `chain` the id of the root ask of its chain, `hop` its depth (0 at the root) and `cross_hops` how many asks of the chain crossed to another Mac. Money is in micro-dollars (US$1 = 1000000) at API prices; `cost_micro_usd` is null for an ask from before costs were kept. `cap_micro_usd` is the chain cap in force now (null: none). `capped_ms` is when this ask's run took its chain to that cap, and `cap_card_ms` when the host raised the Needs-you card for it (once per chain and cap). Times are ms. A record from before delegation records reads as a root ask: chain = its id, hop 0. `brief` is the ask's text (at most 2000 characters) and `session` the asked agent's session once a --bg run claimed one; both are for the owner's peek, null on an older record, and never part of a member's or bot's RPC.

Caller.description: Who asked: the agent (null for a terminal), the person whose run it is (null for the owner) and where it came from (`terminal`, `serve`, ...).

ReplyTo.description: Where the answer goes: the caller's session (a wake once nobody waits for it) and the ask whose run asked. This is the only place the address lives; cards never carry it.

KernelVersion.description: `kith kernel version`: the interface version and the modules this build answers.

Engines.description: `kith kernel engines --json`: the coding engines, installed or not, as the engine table describes them.

LaunchPrompt.description: `kith kernel launch prompt --json`: the system prompt a run gets.
